findings.headline: High stress on lap 9 did not affect pace – mental load from rain forecast, not tyre wear.
findings.detail: Stress spiked to 61.7 on lap 9 while the driver was on medium tyres (age 9) in dry conditions, fighting traffic (P8, 0.7s gap) and received a rain forecast. Pace delta was -0.170 s, indicating no loss despite high stress. The model suggests the medium tyre was still within its performance window, so the stress was likely mental (rain anticipation) rather than tyre‑related.

findings.headline: Intermediate tyre degradation caused a 3.6 s slowdown under blue flags; fresh intermediates restored pace.
findings.detail: From laps 23‑25 on intermediate tyres the pace delta jumped to +3.646 s on lap 25 while the driver was under blue flags and the track was wet. The modelled degradation for the intermediate stint (+0.815 s/lap) aligns with the large slowdown, indicating the tyre was losing grip. Switching to fresh intermediates at lap 28 recovered pace (‑2.348 s on lap 29).

findings.headline: Soft tyres performed consistently through the wet‑dry transition, no pace loss.
findings.detail: During the wet‑to‑dry crossover at lap 40 the driver stayed on soft tyres (age 3) and maintained a flat pace delta (+0.000). The model suggests the softs were still optimal (+0.028 s/lap overall) and the driver handled the drying line without losing time, despite blue flags on lap 40‑41.

findings.headline: Low stress on lap 16 coincided with an ageing medium tyre; monitor for degradation before next stop.
findings.detail: Stress dropped to 30.1 on lap 16 while the driver was on medium tyres (age 16) on a clear track, with a 5.9 s gap to the car ahead. Pace delta was flat (+0.000), indicating the driver was relaxed but the tyre was already modelled as past its optimal window (medium stint degradation +0.103 s/lap). No immediate performance hit, but the tyre may have been nearing the limit for the next stint.

findings.headline: Soft tyre pace variation late race driven by surface changes, not tyre degradation.
findings.detail: From lap 45 to 51 on soft tyres the pace delta fluctuated (+0.000 to +0.745 s) while the track alternated between wet and dry and blue flags appeared intermittently. The modelled soft degradation (+0.028 s/lap) is small, so the variability is likely due to changing surface conditions rather than tyre wear.
evidence: track wet on lap 45, dry on 46‑51
